The EU AI Act addresses data protection and transparency obligations for companies using AI systems by integrating these requirements into its regulatory framework. It complements existing data protection regulations, such as the GDPR, ensuring that when AI systems process personal data, the GDPR remains fully applicable. This includes obligations related to automated decisions with significant effects, transparency, purpose limitation, data minimization, and privacy by design.

Specifically, the AI Act introduces risk-based obligations that vary depending on the role of the company (provider or deployer) and the risk classification of the AI system. For high-risk AI systems, companies must conduct risk assessments, maintain high-quality datasets, provide extensive documentation, and ensure transparency by adequately informing users about the AI system's operation and potential risks. This includes disclosing foreseeable risks to health, safety, or fundamental rights, thereby linking transparency directly to the protection of fundamental rights. 

Overall, the AI Act emphasizes that transparency is not merely an afterthought but a fundamental design feature of high-risk AI systems, aimed at empowering users and ensuring accountability.
